extracted.intended_audience: registrants, corporate accountants, auditors, and securities counsel preparing SEC filings for business acquisitions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for the form, content, periods, age, and filing of financial statements (and related disclosures) of an acquired business under Regulation S‑X (Rule 3‑05) and related SEC rules, including Form 8‑K filing obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes in stockholders' equity and noncontrolling interests (S-X Rule 3-04)
rubrics_metrics.description: An analysis of the changes in each caption of stockholders' equity and noncontrolling interests presented in the balance sheets shall be given in a note or separate statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present as a reconciliation of the beginning balance to the ending balance for each period for which a statement of comprehensive income is required, with all significant reconciling items described by appropriate captions; contributions from and distributions to owners shown separately; state separately adjustments to the beginning balance of the earliest period presented for items retrospectively applied to prior periods; for dividends, state the amount per share and in the aggregate for each class of shares; provide a separate schedule in the notes that shows the effects of any changes in the registrant's ownership interest in a subsidiary on the equity attributable to the registrant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smaller reporting company annual financial statements (S-X Rule 8-02)
rubrics_metrics.description: Smaller reporting companies shall file an audited balance sheet as of the end of each of the most recent two fiscal years (or as of a date within 135 days if issuer existed for <1 year), and audited statements of comprehensive income, cash flows and changes in stockholders' equity for each of the two fiscal years preceding the date of the most recent audited balance sheet (or such shorter period as the registrant has been in business).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim financial statements – review and required content (S-X Rule 8-03)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim financial statements may be unaudited; however, interim financial statements included in quarterly reports on Form 10‑Q must be reviewed by an independent public accountant using applicable professional standards and procedures; if the issuer states interim statements have been reviewed, a report of the accountant on the review must be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim financial statements shall include a balance sheet as of the end of the issuer's most recent fiscal quarter, a balance sheet as of the end of the preceding fiscal year, and statements of comprehensive income and statements of cash flows for the interim period up to the date of such balance sheet and the comparable period of the preceding fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condensed interim financial statements format and minimum line items
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim financial statements may be presented in condensed format subject to specific line item and caption requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1) Balance sheets: include separate captions for each balance sheet component presented in the annual financial statements that represents 10% or more of total assets; cash and retained earnings presented regardless of relative significance; if annual statements are classified, present totals for current assets and current liabilities. (2) Statements of comprehensive income: include net sales or gross revenue, each cost and expense category presented in the annual financial statements that exceeds 20% of sales or gross revenues, provision for income taxes, and discontinued operations (financial institutions substitute net interest income for sales). (3) Cash flow statements: include cash flows from operating, investing and financing activities as well as cash at beginning and end of each period and the increase or decrease in such balance. (4) Additional line items may be presented to facilitate usefulness and comparability. (5) Provide information required by §210.3‑04 for current and comparative year‑to‑date periods with subtotals for each interim period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnote and other disclosures for interim statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnote and other disclosures should be provided as needed for fair presentation and to ensure that the financial statements are not misleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure for significant equity investees in interim statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Sales, gross profit, net income (loss) from continuing operations, net income, and net income attributable to the investee must be disclosed for equity investees that constitute 20% or more of a registrant's consolidated assets, equity or income from continuing operations attributable to the registrant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material accounting changes – auditor letter and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The registrant's independent accountant must provide a letter in the first Form 10‑Q filed after a change indicating whether or not the change is to a preferable method; disclosure must be provided of any retroactive change to prior period financial statements, including the effect on income and income per share.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial statements and disclosures about guarantors and issuers of guaranteed securities
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial statements and disclosures for guarantors and issuers of guaranteed securities are subject to the requirements of §210.3‑10 and disclosures must be presented as required by §210.13‑01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosures about affiliates whose securities collateralize an issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosures about a registrant's affiliates whose securities collateralize any class of securities registered or being registered and the related collateral arrangement must be presented as required by §210.13‑02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim quarter reporting when Article 8 applies (Instruction 1 to §210.8‑03)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where Articles 8‑01 through 8‑08 are applicable to a Form 10‑Q and the interim period is more than one quarter, statements of comprehensive income must also be provided for the most recent interim quarter and the comparable quarter of the preceding fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Components of Rule 3‑05 financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: S‑X Rule 3‑05 requires consolidated balance sheets (as specified in Rule 3‑01); consolidated statements of comprehensive income and cash flows (as specified in Rule 3‑02); and a statement of changes in stockholders' equity (presented in either a note or separate statement as specified in Rule 3‑04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Periods required depend on acquisition significance (Rule 3‑05 periods table)
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of annual and interim periods of audited financial statements of an acquired business required in a filing depends on the acquisition's significance relative to the registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary: If acquisition does not exceed 20% — none; exceeds 20% but not 40% — one fiscal year; exceeds 40% — two fiscal years (with interim period subsequent to the required annual period and comparative interim period requirements described). For individually insignificant acquisitions that aggregate >50% significance, audited financial statements are required for entities >20% individually if not previously provided, and most recent unaudited interim period for entities >20% individually if not previously provided. A period of less than a year may satisfy the annual requirement under S‑X Rule 3‑06 in some cases. Special circumstances (e.g., securities offered to acquired shareholders in certain filings; acquired business previously included in registrant's consolidated statements) can affect annual period requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro‑forma information requirements (S‑X Article 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pro forma financial information is required when a significant acquisition has occurred in the most recent fiscal year or subsequent interim period, or is probable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically includes the most recent (annual or interim) balance sheet and annual and interim income statements showing how the acquisition might have affected those financial statements if transaction occurred earlier. If the acquired entity is already included in such balance sheet, the most recent pro forma balance sheet is not required. Pro forma information is not required for individually insignificant acquisitions unless they are >50% significant in the aggregate. See Article 11 and chapter 2 for further discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age of financial statements – definition and controlling rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'age of financial statements' refers to which periods the Rule 3‑05 financial statements to be filed must cover; the timing of the acquisition and the related filing date drive the age determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two rules address age: S‑X Rule 3‑01 (general age requirements) and S‑X Rule 3‑12 (updating financial statements required in a filing). SRC age requirements are in S‑X Rule 8‑08, which generally result in the same determinations. The type of filing establishes a specific date important to determine age (e.g., for Form 8‑K, registration statement, proxy materials).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual financial statements required and 'specific date' exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide audited annual financial statements from the acquired business's most recent fiscal year(s) required by Rule 3‑01; generally the most recently completed fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the specific date identified (see age rules) falls 'shortly after' the acquired business's most recently completed fiscal year, the prior fiscal year may satisfy the requirement. If audited financial statements for the most recently completed fiscal year are available, they must be included even if the prior year would meet age requirements. Two years may be required depending on acquisition significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim financial statements required – timing and dating rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim period financials are required depending on acquisition significance, timing of acquisition, and the type of filing; they are required if the required annual period financial statements are dated 135 (or 130) days or more before the relevant filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If interim financials are provided they must be dated fewer than 135 (or 130) days before the relevant filing date. Examples and timelines illustrate required interim periods for Form 8‑K filings. See Questions 4.3.10 and 4.4.30 for application to Form 8‑K and registration statements/proxy materials respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 3‑05 financial statements must comply with Reg S‑X and US GAAP for a PBE
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 3‑05 financial statements need to comply with Reg S‑X and US GAAP requirements for a public business entity (PBE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acquired‑business entities whose financial statements are included in an SEC filing are considered PBEs and therefore may not use Private Company Council (PCC) accounting alternatives (e.g., amortization of goodwill) and must apply public company transition provisions for new standards except in certain circumstances (e.g., an EGC). Financial statements of a PBE are presented as if the company had always been public; historical interim and annual statements not prepared on that basis must be retrospectively revised for inclusion. Financial information used to determine significance must also be based on PBE requirements. Certain disclosures that apply only to public entities under specific Topics may not be required for nonpublic acquired businesses (see separate criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosures not required for nonpublic acquired businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain information and disclosures required by various accounting standards are not required for nonpublic acquired businesses or acquired businesses that do not have publicly held common stock or potential common stock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of Topics with disclosures not required: Topic 260 (earnings per share), Topic 280 (segment reporting), Topic 715 (retirement benefits). This is not an exhaustive list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental schedules and industry guide disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedules otherwise required by S‑X Articles 5 and 12 need not be furnished for significant acquired businesses, except schedules required by S‑X Rule 6‑11 for acquired funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEC staff may require inclusion in a note or elsewhere in the filing of information ordinarily furnished in the schedules when it would be material to understanding the financial statements of the acquired business. Industry guide and other Reg S‑K industry‑specific disclosures are not required by S‑X Rule 3‑05 even if the acquiree operates in such industries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of Staff Accounting Bulletins (SABs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance of Rule 3‑05 financial statements with Reg S‑X includes consideration and application of various SABs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: consider SAB Topic 1N relative to the evaluation of errors under the dual method. See relevant SABs for guidance on particular accounting issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances requiring PCAOB audit and auditor registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 3‑05 financial statements of a non‑issuer entity are not required to include an auditors' report under PCAOB standards and auditors of non‑issuers are not required to register with the PCAOB; however, Rule 3‑05 financial statements of an issuer entity are required to be audited under PCAOB standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The KPMG text lists scenarios and staff views indicating when an auditor's report must reference PCAOB standards and when the auditor must be a PCAOB‑registered firm (e.g., issuer and its predecessor; entities filing an initial registration statement; certain SPAC predecessor situations). Auditors' reports that contain qualifications due to audit scope limitations (or disclaimers) do not satisfy the requirement for the financial statements to be 'audited' because the auditor was unable to perform all necessary procedures (see SAB Topic 1E(2)). Consider auditor independence and related issues in reverse merger and SPAC scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auditors' review requirement for Rule 3‑05 interim statements in special cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 3‑05 interim financial statements need not be reviewed by an independent public accountant unless the acquired business is the accounting acquirer or the predecessor of the registrant acquirer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pushdown accounting optionality and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no requirement or prohibition to applying pushdown accounting in financial statements filed with the SEC if it is permitted by US GAAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If pushdown accounting is applied, the separate stand‑alone financial statements of the acquired business reflect the recorded acquisition adjustments pushed down; when elected, income/comprehensive income, cash flows and changes in stockholders' equity for the year that includes the change in control often include predecessor and successor periods separated by a vertical line and labeled Predecessor/Successor, with notes including relevant information separated for the predecessor and successor periods. If not elected, there is no split between predecessor and successor periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviated financial statements under Rule 3‑05(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: Abbreviated financial statements may be provided to satisfy Rule 3‑05 requirements when net assets that constitute a business are acquired and certain qualifying conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See further discussion and qualifying conditions in chapter 10; S‑X Rule 3‑05(e) governs abbreviated statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 8‑K Item 2.01 — definition of 'significant' acquisition (instruction to Form 8‑K)
rubrics_metrics.description: An acquisition or disposition will be deemed to involve a significant amount of assets if: (i) the registrant's and its subsidiaries' equity in the net book value of such assets or the amount paid/received exceeded 10% of total assets; (ii) it involved a business that is significant (see 17 CFR 210.11‑01(d)); or (iii) for a business development company, the amount paid exceeded 10% of value of total investments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The aggregate impact of acquired businesses need not be reported pursuant to Item 2.01 unless they are related businesses, related real estate operations, or related funds and are significant in the aggregate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 8‑K Item 9.01 — filing of acquired business financial statements and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: For any business acquisition required to be described in Item 2.01, file financial statements and any applicable supplemental information of the business acquired specified in Rules 3‑05 or 3‑14 or Rules 8‑04/8‑06 for SRCs or Rule 6‑11 for funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1) Financial statements must be prepared pursuant to Regulation S‑X though supporting schedules need not be filed unless required by Rule 6‑11. (2) A manually signed accountant's report should be provided pursuant to Rule 2‑02 of Regulation S‑X. (3) Financial statements required by Item 9.01 may be filed with the initial report or by amendment not later than 71 calendar days after the date the initial Form 8‑K must be filed; if not included in initial report, registrant should indicate when they will be filed. Registrant may include unaudited financial statements in the initial Form 8‑K at its option.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Instruction B.3 — previously reported information and incorporation by reference
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant previously has reported substantially the same information as required by Form 8‑K, the registrant need not make an additional report of the information on this form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To the extent an item calls for disclosure of developments concerning a previously reported event or transaction, any information required in the new report or amendment about the previously reported event or transaction may be provided by incorporation by reference to the previously filed report. 'Previously reported' is defined in Rule 12b‑2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 8‑K periods and age determination (timing rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: The age of the financial statements of an acquired business to be included in a Form 8‑K is determined by reference to the earlier of (a) the date the Form 8‑K is initially filed or (b) the due date of the Form 8‑K reporting the acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Form 8‑K reporting the acquisition must be filed on or before the fourth business day following the date of the acquisition's consummation. Registrants may file the required financial statements of the acquired business with this initial Form 8‑K or use a 71‑day extension period to file Rule 3‑05 financial statements by later amending the Form 8‑K.
